notes.trap: It tests only whether the key exists. A key whose value is NULL still returns true, while `map[key]` returns NULL both for a missing key and for a present key with a NULL value. A NULL map gives NULL, not false.

Under the default spark.sql.mapKeyDedupPolicy=EXCEPTION, building a map with a duplicate key fails instead of keeping the last value. So `map_keys(...)` over such a map never returns de-duplicated keys; the query errors.
notes.actual: ERROR: SparkRuntimeException DUPLICATED_MAP_KEY :: [DUPLICATED_MAP_KEY] Duplicate map key 1 was found, please check the input data. If you want to remove the duplicated keys, you can set "spark.sql.mapKeyDedupPolicy" to "LAST_WIN" so that the key inserted at last takes precedence.

notes.trap: It returns an array of structs with fields named `key` and `value`. Bracket subscripts on that array are 0-based, unlike the 1-based `element_at(...)`.
Map keys can never be NULL, but values can. The array returned by `map_values(...)` keeps NULL elements, which print as lowercase `null` when the array is cast to a string.
notes.example_sql: SELECT CAST(map_values(map(1, CAST(NULL AS STRING))) AS STRING)
